subject: Architecture
title: Fire Engineering: Beyond Escape Routes
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fire Engineering: Beyond Escape Routes usable.

hook.text: The Grenfell Tower fire in 2017 killed 72 people in London — because flammable cladding turned the exterior into fuel.

buildup.text: Aluminum composite panels with polyethylene cores had been added during renovation — a cheap, combustible choice.

discovery.text: Fire spread up the outside of the building in minutes — bypassing all internal fire compartment barriers.

twist.text: Residents were told to 'stay put' — standard advice for compartmented fires, but deadly when the exterior is burning.

climax.text: Countries worldwide banned combustible cladding and began inspecting thousands of high-rises for the same panels.

punchline.text: A £10 million renovation to save money. 72 lives lost to save pennies per panel.

quiz.question: What made the Grenfell Tower fire so deadly?
options: The building had no fire exits or emergency stairs
Flammable exterior cladding spread fire up the outside
Arson accelerants were found on multiple floors

details.summary: Fire engineering has evolved far beyond simple escape routes. Modern buildings use compartmentalization, smoke management systems, fire-resistant materials, and active suppression to control fires rather than just evacuate occupants.
details.whyItMatters: The Grenfell Tower fire killed 72 people partly because flammable cladding bypassed fire compartmentalization. It showed that fire engineering fails when economic pressure overrides safety specifications — a systemic risk in cost-driven construction.
takeaways: Modern fire engineering uses compartmentalization and active suppression
The Grenfell Tower fire exposed dangerous compromises in fire safety
Fire engineering fails when cost-cutting overrides safety specifications

faq.question: What went wrong at Grenfell Tower?
faq.answer: Flammable ACM cladding was installed over the building's exterior, creating a continuous fuel source that bypassed internal fire compartmentalization. Fire spread up the outside of the building in minutes, entering apartments through windows. The stay-put evacuation policy became a death trap.

faq.question: What is fire compartmentalization?
faq.answer: Dividing a building into fire-resistant zones that contain a fire to its room or floor of origin, buying time for evacuation and firefighting. Walls, floors, and doors are rated to resist fire for 30-120 minutes.
